prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the supplied 4x4 exercise contact sheet; keep exactly the same grid, woman, face, torso, framing, backdrop, mat, dumbbell and hand in ALL cells. Correct the leg poses only, to make a small slow march in place with genuinely different intermediate heights. DO NOT increase the knee height. One right leg lift returns to the floor fully, then one left leg lift returns fully. The dumbbell always stays in her anatomical right hand, on the LEFT side of the picture, and never moves to the other hand.
Panel numbers describe cells, retain their small numbers unchanged.
Make these exact corrections:
Panel1: keep both feet grounded.
Panel2: right shoe barely lifted 2 cm, LEFT shoe grounded.
Panel3: right shoe lifted 6 cm, LEFT shoe grounded. This must be MUCH LOWER than the current high-knee panel3.
Panel4: right shoe lifted 12 cm, LEFT shoe grounded.
Panel5: right shoe lifted 18 cm (the highest for this modest march), LEFT shoe grounded.
Panel6: right shoe descending at 10 cm, LEFT shoe grounded.
Panel7: right shoe descending at 3 cm, LEFT shoe grounded.
Panel8: both feet grounded in the same locations as panel1.
Panel9: LEFT shoe barely lifted 2 cm, RIGHT shoe grounded.
Panel10: LEFT shoe lifted 6 cm, RIGHT shoe grounded. The currently raised leg in panel10 is WRONG; change to the other leg, viewer RIGHT.
Panel11: LEFT shoe lifted 12 cm, RIGHT shoe grounded.
Panel12: LEFT shoe lifted 18 cm, RIGHT shoe grounded.
Panel13: LEFT shoe lowering at 10 cm, RIGHT shoe grounded.
Panel14: LEFT shoe lowering at 3 cm, RIGHT shoe grounded.
Panels15 and16: both feet grounded exactly like panel1.
For every raised foot the knee is softly bent with shin hanging naturally; thighs never approach horizontal. Grounded shoes are flat and NEVER slide or jump side to side. Hip-width stance, consistent two separate foot landing locations. Torso and pelvis upright and level, no leaning, no body elongation, no zoom. Keep the entire subject visible and the scale identical in every panel. The result should communicate modest controlled foot lifts, not exaggerated high knees. Do not change any colors or add texture.
